Use case: stylized-concept / constrained spacecraft design exploration.
ONE new li_pir_elite concept sheet. The owner wants ten genuinely different construction studies of a FORWARD-FACING ANUBIS/ORDER TAIL WITH A DEVELOPED SOLID PEDESTAL. This call makes only the specified variant. Each changes the tail base and mass distribution, not the whole ship. The last thin hook-like fin was rejected. A short broad plinth, credible structural transitions and a substantial stepped tail body are essential.

INPUT ROLES:
1. L66: preserve its successful broad hull, two compact horizontally separated engine shoulders, maintained pirate Liberty materials and closed roof. Its existing thin tail and two-leaf wings are NOT to be copied: replace them as specified. Do not reinstate any transverse bar over engines.
2. IMMUTABLE original cabin and collar: actual low glass capsule, same pane outlines/shell, original proportions and all three angular collar ribs with visible gaps. No canopy redesign or added brow.
3. ACTUAL DEFENDER COMPONENT GEOMETRY: primary reference for the WING EMERGENCE POINT and original three-leaf fan. Ignore display colors and native old spoiler/vertical engines. Copy the root at the LOWER FRONT EDGE OF THE MAIN HULL, below the long side decorative field, where the inclined lower flank begins AFTER the short neck behind the collar. The wings do NOT attach to the collar itself, cockpit shell, upper roof, tail pedestal or aft engine pod. Maintain the source's small but visible separation between the collar's back and the wing hinge. No forward-shifted hinge glued to a collar rib. No new external support arm.
4. Actual or_elite / Anubis: PRIMARY TAIL CONSTRUCTION reference. Study the deep stepped lower body, broad longitudinal footing, substantial middle mass and solid tapered upper blade. Reverse this integrated tail's FORE-AFT DIRECTION so its upper mass points toward the cockpit. Do not copy Order's cabin, engines, wing roots, colors or complete hull.
5. Actual pirate Defender: original THREE angular fan leaves, materials, native wing roots and restrained equipment distribution. Maintain these wings and their normal origin rather than the previous AI root placement.

LOCKED WINGS:
Exactly THREE complete pointed angular plates per side at the native Defender lower-front flank roots described above. Six moving leaves total. Native inclined fan plane, separate free tips and actual overlap thickness. One ordinary native weapon plate per fan, not one giant mounting plate on each of three leaves. Restore the ordinary source contours. All three fold backward/inward along the lower flank without shrinking. Preserve their native longitudinal origin in SIDE and TOP. The redesigned rear motor shoulders remain above the folded wing packet.

TAIL FOUNDATION, THE MAIN DESIGN SUBJECT:
The tail is an integrated three-dimensional stern assembly, not a paper-thin fin or a hook on a narrow stalk. Build a distinct SOLID FIXED PEDESTAL with appreciable fore-aft length, transverse width, side faces and upper mounting shoulders. It visibly joins the central aft bulkhead between the engines, aft of the working hatch, and carries the thick lower tail structure. Make the original Order's interesting foundation legible from both front-side and REAR 3/4. No pointed blade rising directly out of the flat roof; no skinny ankle or unsupported top overhang.
Above the pedestal, two closely overlapping full-size polygonal tail sections may fold via modest slide/pivot as in the existing L66 idea; do not erase or lay the whole structure flat. Broad overlapping faces and integrated closed joint seats, not exposed rods. This motion is a proposal requiring geometry checks.
There must be NO HOOK shape, C-shaped neck, spear tip, horn, projecting little beak, thin horizontal cap over empty space, or ornamental temple tower. Instead use a thick FORWARD-RISING stepped WEDGE / BLADE with a blunt clipped top and a continuous substantial connection into its pedestal. A small seam between moving sections is fine; a big open undercut is not.
FORWARD means toward the cabin. In SIDE nose LEFT, the upper tail mass must be LEFT of the lower tail-root center. In a rear perspective with the cockpit on the RIGHT, upper mass must lean RIGHT. Never reverse the whole ship to fake this. The long sloped flank and stepped buttress are the Order tail reversed, not just a pointed fin reversed.
Place restrained functional equipment mounting flats on the pedestal's lateral faces and the tail's thick section, away from the top surfaces of the engines. No installed guns or extra engine. Keep both engine service housings plain and separate, without a connecting spoiler. Keep all new tail structure behind the flush hatch footprint; no long front foot over the doors. The central roof stays filled and broadly flat, with no trough or raised longitudinal sidewalls.

STYLE:
Preserve L66's recognizably functional Liberty ship and its native red/ochre/pale materials. Main identity is the exposed original ribbed collar. Native Art Deco/Empire panels support the construction, do not turn it into palace sculpture. Mild wear only, no wreck damage, heavy rust, skeletons, pipes, flags, skulls or spikes. Spend design change on connected large and medium volumes, not micro-detail.

PRESENTATION:
Clean grey studio concept sheet. TWO large useful views: front-side 3/4, nose LEFT, and REAR 3/4 showing both engines, tail pedestal and wing roots. Orient BOTH large images with the cockpit toward the LEFT: in REAR 3/4 the cockpit is farther away at upper LEFT, and the two exhausts are nearer at lower RIGHT. This keeps the FORWARD tail lean toward the LEFT in both perspectives; do not simply reuse the opposite-facing rear camera from the AI reference. Below: SIDE FLIGHT nose LEFT, TOP, straight REAR, SIDE STOWED nose LEFT. Consistent shape, proportions, root location and forward tail direction in all views. Native three-leaf wings visibly nest in stowed view; tail remains substantial with slight nesting. Ordinary-size cabin, long lens. Labels only ID and view names, no text paragraphs.
